Abstract—This is a pilot study that develops a force -sensor 
interface circuit in the fo rm of a strip to continuously monitor 
the patient's heart rate. Strip force sensors have been developed 
to measure forces generated from body movements using 
polyvinylidene fluoride films. The interface circuit is specially 
designed to have low frequency r esponse considering slow body 
motion and confirmed by SPICE simulation. 
. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
To diagnose sleep disorder, polysomnography is used as 
the gold standard for sleep monitoring. However, this method 
is necessary for the subject to sleep with a large nu mber of 
sensors attached. To overcome these disadvantages, we 
developed a new sensor in our previous research [1]. But the 
performance of the sensor interface circuit developed in our 
study is vulnerable to noise, and therefore, it is necessary to 
improve the signal to noise ratio. In particular, it must have a 
lower frequency passband to detect breathing and heart rate. 
In this paper, we intend to design a new interface circuit 
through SPICE simulation in order to improve the 
performance of the sensor int erface circuit d eveloped in the 
previous research. 
II. METHODS 
An equivalent model of the strip-type force sensor to be 
used in the interface circuit design was obtained. Th e 
strip-type force sensor is modeled as a voltage source with a 
series capacitor and re sistor. In this case, the capacitance 
value was repeatedly measured using a digital multimeter 
(U1271A, Agilent co.). At this time, the resistance value was 
set to 1 giga-ohm. The op amp model used in the circuit design 
simulation is OPA337, and it is desi gned based on th e 
differential charge mode to eliminate the common noise 
flowing between the sensor and the interface circuit. The 
simulation is performed by Texas instrument TINA ver. 9 was 
used.

We selected the value of R f as 500 mega -ohm and the 
value of C f as 330 pico farad empirically. The lower cutoff 
frequency was 0.96 Hz and the charge gain of the interface 
circuit was approximately 12 dB. The simulation results of 
the strip -type force sensor and interfacing circuit and 
Equivalent model for the strip -type force sensor were shown 
in Fig. 1. 
III. RESULTS 
In order to improve the sensor interface circuit developed 
in the previous research, we designed the differential charge 
amplifier through simulation. The designed circuit is expected 
to improve the signal to noise ratio of the measurement signals 
of breathing and heartbeat during sleep.
